Quality is a first-class priority for us, not a phase at the end. You'll work closely with developers, Product, Customer Support and your Engineering Manager. What you'll own in your first year Own: Own quality for a service or product area end to end — test strategy, automation, release sign-off, and follow-up on escaped bugs. Test strategy. Decide what to automate, what to test by hand, and what risk is acceptable for each release. Automation that lasts. Build and extend API, UI and integration test suites that are fast, reliable and run in CI on every change. Shift left. Review designs and requirements early, and work with developers so testability is built in, not bolted on. Learn from escapes. When a bug reaches customers, find out why and close the gap so it doesn't happen again. Raise the bar. Review test code, mentor SDET-1s, and help interview candidates. Ownership, curiosity, and a willingness to learn. description: For nearly 40 years, PDI has helped convenience retailers and petroleum wholesalers adapt to changes in the industry by leveraging the latest technologies. The result is unparalleled insights, simplified operations, and higher profitability for your employees and business. We’re dedicated to helping our more than 1,500 customers in over 50 countries, providing solutions and services to over 200,000 sites. PDI C-Store Essentials is cloud back-office software for convenience store owners and operators. It covers pricebook and promotions, point-of-sale integration, fuel, lottery, daily paperwork, scan data reporting and subscription billing, for single stores, chains and franchise operators. You will build and maintain features across the Essentials web application, its .NET services and its databases, as part of a team split between India and the United States. The team works AI-first: coding agents are part of how every engineer plans, builds, tests and reviews work, and this role is expected to use them well from day one. Job Responsibilities: Design, build and ship features across the stack: React and TypeScript on the front end, ASP.NET Core services and APIs on the back end, SQL Server and PostgreSQL underneath Take part in design decisions for new and existing features, raise risks early and ask for help when blocked Work with the Product Owner to clarify requirements, break them into small deliverable pieces and estimate them Write automated tests for your own work (xUnit, Vitest, Playwright) and work with QA engineers on test plans and release stabilization. Troubleshoot and fix development and production issues with urgency, using logs and monitoring to find the root cause. Review teammates' pull requests and respond to review on your own. Keep documentation of what you build current, including the instructions and context that coding agents rely on Give your manager clear status and risk updates so work stays on schedule. AI-driven development (AIDLC) The team follows an AI-driven development lifecycle (AIDLC): coding agents take part in every stage of delivery, and engineers direct, check and own the result. This is a core requirement of the role, not a preference. You will be expected to: Use coding agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor every day, across requirements, design, implementation, testing, code review and debugging. Turn a user story into a clear, bounded task an agent can carry out: the goal, the constraints, the files and data involved, and how success will be checked. Plan before generating: have the agent propose an approach, challenge it, and agree the design before code is written. Verify everything an agent produces. Read the diff, run the tests, exercise the change in the running application, and reject work you cannot explain. Own what you merge. Code written by an agent is held to the same standard as code written by hand, and you answer for it in review and in production. Keep credentials, customer data and other sensitive information out of prompts and agent context, and follow PDI's AI usage policies. Improve the team's shared setup: project instructions, reusable prompts and skills, test fixtures and other context that make agents more reliable for everyone. Know when not to use an agent and recognize when one is going in circles or producing plausible but wrong output. Self-starter who can work independently as part of a distributed team, manage competing priorities and learn an unfamiliar codebase quickly.
